doc.title: Benny Waters interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995

title: Starting out on piano, trumpet, clarinet and sax; his musical brothers
summary: Waters says he was born playing at three, moved through piano, trumpet, clarinets and sax; his brothers played brass and other instruments, his sisters none.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: How did you get started in music?

In music? Well I’m a protégé, I was, that’s maybe not the right word in English because I’ve been in France so long. Anyway, I was born playing, like a gift from God, see, at three years old. So I was playing the piano then, so then after I stopped playing the piano, I went to the trumpet. But my lips got so sore that I gave it up right quick. Then I went to clarinet — E flat clarinet — and I did band music and concert music. Then from the E flat clarinet to the B flat clarinet. And then on to the saxophone, on like that.
Everyone in your family was musical, weren’t they?

Well no, all the brothers were. My brother, my oldest brother was quite a virtuoso. He played all of the wind instruments, rather all of the brass instruments like the tuba and the trombone and the trumpet. He majored on the trumpet, but he could play all the brass instruments and could play clarinet also. And he played a little flute and oboe. He was quite a virtuoso. And the other brother played trombone, and the other one played the, I © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-
guess they called it a mellophone or something, I forget what the name of that thing is in the military band, see. But the sisters didn’t, they didn’t play anything, my sisters.
